summary: PBDB supplies today's first-appearance ages per genus and family, entry and modification dates for every occurrence, and the reference text (with year) for each, so range changes can be examined against when records were entered or published. What it does not provide is a dated series of earlier compilations or database releases, and no deposit of historic first-appearance datums was found in DataCite, Dryad or Zenodo.
next_step: Either use PBDB record-creation dates and reference years as a proxy for discovery order, or locate and digitize earlier compilations (e.g. Sepkoski-era lists) and pre-register how entry date substitutes for discovery date; sampling intensity below each first appearance would come from PBDB/Macrostrat collections.
obstacles_confirmed: No dated snapshots of earlier compilations were found.
PBDB entry dates reflect database curation, not discovery dates.
Absence below a first appearance cannot be separated from non-preservation by data alone.
